map.People never change their behavior, what: People are motivated by how fairly their pay compares with what coworkers receive for similar jobs
map.People work only for fear of losing the: People are motivated by a need to satisfy basic needs first and then move up to higher needs

ww.People are motivated by how fairly their: That describes equity theory, which is about fairness comparisons. Expectancy theory links motivation to beliefs that effort leads to performance and performance to valued rewards.
ww.People are motivated by a need to satisf: That describes a needs hierarchy. Expectancy theory is about beliefs that effort leads to performance and that performance leads to rewards people value.

map.Rewards do not matter to workers, who ca: People are motivated by clear goals that are specific and challenging, with feedback on progress
map.Only managers matter in the firm, since: People are motivated by the work itself, such as responsibility and achievement, more than by pay

ww.People are motivated by clear goals that: That describes goal-setting theory. Equity theory is about workers comparing their inputs and rewards with those of others and seeking fairness.
ww.People are motivated by the work itself,: That describes a job-content view of motivation. Equity theory is about comparing inputs and rewards with others and seeking fairness.

map.They are always identical, so a legal ac: Legal rules come from a firm, while ethics come from the courts
map.Legal means always right, and no legal a: Ethics are written laws, while legal rules are personal views

ww.Legal rules come from a firm, while ethi: Laws are made by governments, not individual firms, and ethics reflect moral standards. The real difference is that a legal act can still be judged unethical.
ww.Ethics are written laws, while legal rul: This swaps the terms. Laws are formal rules set by government, while ethics are moral standards, so a legal act can still be considered unethical.

map.Ignoring them and their progress entirel: Having a manager approve each decision
map.Checking their work every hour of the da: Replacing them with newer, cheaper hires

ww.Having a manager approve each decision: Approving each decision is a directive style that suits novices. Experienced engineers do their best work when trusted to choose their own methods.
ww.Replacing them with newer, cheaper hires: Replacing skilled staff discards proven experience. Experienced engineers work best when a leader delegates and lets them choose how to solve problems.

map.Give her no feedback or any coaching at: Move her to a different team each month
map.Keep her in the same job forever so that: Offer a one-time raise and no new duties

ww.Move her to a different team each month: Frequent moves prevent her from building depth or finishing projects. Development needs stretch assignments with regular coaching and feedback.
ww.Offer a one-time raise and no new duties: A raise adds no new skills or experience. Preparing her for a future role needs challenging assignments and ongoing coaching.

map.They are exactly the same thing in every: Motivation is a short-term bonus plan, while inspiration is a long-term pay raise
map.Motivation comes only from pay, and insp: Motivation comes from outside rewards, while inspiration is a formal training program

ww.Motivation is a short-term bonus plan, w: Neither is a pay scheme. Motivation drives action toward goals, and inspiration lifts people's sense of purpose.
ww.Motivation comes from outside rewards, w: Motivation can come from outside rewards or inner drives, and inspiration is a lift in purpose, not a training program.

map.Managers never plan or organize, while l: Leaders handle daily scheduling and budgets, while managers write the company's vision
map.Leaders only follow orders, while manage: Managers are appointed by rank, while leaders are chosen by their followers

ww.Leaders handle daily scheduling and budg: This swaps the roles. Managers organize and control resources, while leaders set direction, inspire people and drive change.
ww.Managers are appointed by rank, while le: Leaders can hold a formal rank and managers hold one by appointment, so this misstates the difference. Leaders inspire change; managers organize resources.

map.Retention always loses money for the who: Retention spending costs more than it returns, so firms should drop it
map.New customers always cost less than exis: Finding new customers costs about the same as keeping current ones

ww.Retention spending costs more than it re: A $5 return on each $1 spent is a gain, not a loss. Retention here returns more than it costs.
ww.Finding new customers costs about the sa: Winning new customers usually costs more than keeping current ones, and the $5 return shows retention pays; the costs are not the same.

map.Hiding problems from the supplier always: Demanding lower prices after each order

ww.Demanding lower prices after each order: Pushing prices down after each order strains the relationship and signals distrust. Trust grows through reliable payment and open communication.
ww.Sending orders without confirming detail: Skipping confirmation of details causes mistakes and confusion. Trust builds through on-time payment and open communication.

map.They are exactly the same thing and mean: A wage is paid to managers and a salary is paid to part-time staff
map.A wage is paid yearly and a salary is pa: A wage is paid in cash and a salary is paid by check or direct deposit

ww.A wage is paid to managers and a salary: Wage versus salary is not about job rank or part-time status. A wage is paid by the hour, while a salary is a fixed amount per pay period.
ww.A wage is paid in cash and a salary is p: The pay method does not separate them. A wage is paid by the hour, while a salary is a fixed amount per pay period.

map.Ignore every study ever made on the subj: Assume the product works if it is popular
map.Share it widely at once with all of your: Ask the product's seller whether it works

ww.Assume the product works if it is popula: Popularity is not evidence that a product works. A critical thinker looks for the original study and checks its quality.
ww.Ask the product's seller whether it work: A seller has a reason to say yes, so this is not independent evidence. A critical thinker finds the original study and checks its quality.

map.Working only with others in a large grou: Planning tasks on a weekly calendar grid
map.Working only at night, during the late h: Doing the hardest task first each morning

ww.Planning tasks on a weekly calendar grid: Weekly calendar planning is a scheduling method, not Pomodoro. The Pomodoro technique alternates short focused work intervals with brief breaks.
ww.Doing the hardest task first each mornin: Doing the hardest task first is the eat-the-frog method. The Pomodoro technique uses timed, short focused intervals separated by breaks.

map.Quitting every job at the first sign of: Working extra hours to catch up on tasks
map.Taking on even more tasks to stay always: Waiting for the requests to slow down

ww.Working extra hours to catch up on tasks: More hours treat the symptom while the person keeps saying yes. Setting boundaries and politely declining requests addresses overcommitment.
ww.Waiting for the requests to slow down: Requests rarely slow down while the person keeps agreeing. Setting boundaries and saying no politely is the skill that fixes overcommitment.

map.Never, since conflicts solve themselves: Once each side has complained to others
map.Only after one of them has quit the job: After the next annual performance review
map.Only if customers complain about it: When the two employees ask for a transfer

ww.Once each side has complained to others: Waiting until complaints spread means the conflict has already hurt morale and the team. She should step in early, while it is small.
ww.After the next annual performance review: The annual review could be months away, giving the conflict time to harm work and morale. She should step in early.
ww.When the two employees ask for a transfe: Transfer requests mean the conflict has already done damage. Stepping in early prevents harm to work and morale.

map.Forget the goal and carry on as the firm: Repeat last year's budget and wait for results
map.Cut all prices to zero so every customer: Judge the result at year end and then plan

ww.Repeat last year's budget and wait for r: Repeating last year's budget changes nothing about how sales are pursued. After setting a goal, planners develop strategies and action plans to reach it.
ww.Judge the result at year end and then pl: Waiting until year end leaves no way to act toward the goal. The next step is developing strategies and action plans for reaching it.

map.Refuse to discuss changes of any kind an: Approve the features now and tell the client the price will be set after launch
map.Accept every request without question, s: Ask the team to vote on whether to build the features, then inform the client

ww.Approve the features now and tell the cl: Agreeing without pricing or scheduling the work leaves cost and time unclear. The manager should assess the effect on time and cost and agree changes first.
ww.Ask the team to vote on whether to build: A team vote ignores the client's role. Changes need an impact review on time and cost, then agreement with the client before work begins.

map.Lighting always lowers output as workers: Better lighting directly raised output as the main cause
map.Workers dislike teamwork and work better: Strict supervision and close timing raise output most
map.Pay is the only motivator that matters t: Higher wages were the main reason output increased

ww.Better lighting directly raised output a: Output rose even when lighting was reduced, so lighting was not the cause. The studies pointed to attention and social factors.
ww.Strict supervision and close timing rais: The studies did not find strict supervision to be the key. They suggested attention and social factors, including group relationships, lift productivity.
ww.Higher wages were the main reason output: Pay was not the main driver in these studies. Attention and social factors, such as group relationships, improved productivity.

map.The belief that ethics do not exist at a: The view that good actions are those with the best results
map.The belief that only laws matter in busi: The view that moral duties apply to everyone, found through reason

ww.The view that good actions are those wit: That describes consequentialism, which judges actions by outcomes. Ethical relativism holds that right and wrong depend on cultural or personal standards.
ww.The view that moral duties apply to ever: That is a universalist, duty-based view. Relativism holds that moral standards vary with culture or personal views.

map.Judging actions only by their results an: Judging actions by whether they bring the greatest good
map.Doing what is legal only, with no though: Judging actions by the character of the person acting

ww.Judging actions by whether they bring th: That is utilitarianism, a consequence-based view. Deontology judges actions by whether they follow moral duties or rules, regardless of the outcome.
ww.Judging actions by the character of the: That is virtue ethics, which focuses on character. Deontology judges actions by whether they follow moral duties or rules.

map.Structured data is only text while unstr: Structured data is collected by people while unstructured comes from sensors
map.Structured data is always larger than un: Structured data has been cleaned of errors, while unstructured data has not

ww.Structured data is collected by people w: Origin does not separate them. Structured data fits tables with set fields, while unstructured data, such as emails or images, lacks that fixed format.
ww.Structured data has been cleaned of erro: Cleanliness is not the distinction. Structured data fits tables with defined fields; unstructured data, such as images or emails, has no fixed format.

map.Replace every other age in the column wi: Delete the entire column of ages from the data set
map.Leave it as it is because all the data i: Round it down to 100 to keep it realistic

ww.Delete the entire column of ages from th: Dropping the whole column discards many valid ages because of one bad value. The first step is to check whether 250 is an entry error and fix or remove it.
ww.Round it down to 100 to keep it realisti: Changing it to a guessed value invents data without checking the source. The analyst should first check whether it is an entry error, then correct or remove it.

map.A field that is always left blank in eac: A field that links a record to another table
map.A field that repeats in every row with o: A field that holds the largest value in the table

ww.A field that links a record to another t: That is a foreign key, which references a record in another table. A primary key uniquely identifies each record in its own table.
ww.A field that holds the largest value in: Holding the largest value does not identify records. A primary key is a field whose value is unique for each record.

map.It contains only whole numbers and no de: It matches the real-world facts it describes
map.It has never been changed by anyone sinc: It includes a value for each field in the record

ww.It matches the real-world facts it descr: That describes accuracy, not consistency. Consistent data uses the same formats and units across records so values can be compared.
ww.It includes a value for each field in th: That describes completeness. Consistent data uses the same formats, units and conventions across records.

map.Accuracy always equals 50% in a data set: Accuracy falls to near zero when one class dominates
map.Rare classes are never important, so a m: The model must have learned the rare class very well

ww.Accuracy falls to near zero when one cla: Accuracy rises, not falls, in this case, because predicting the common class is correct 99% of the time. That high score hides missed rare cases.
ww.The model must have learned the rare cla: A 99% score does not show that the rare class was learned. A model that always predicts the common class gets 99% while missing each rare case.

map.Software that only edits photographs by: Programs that follow fixed steps to convert files from one format to another
map.Machines that only store large amounts o: Robots that repeat a fixed assembly motion without sensing their surroundings

ww.Programs that follow fixed steps to conv: Converting file formats follows fixed steps with no learning or reasoning. AI means systems that perform tasks usually needing human intelligence.
ww.Robots that repeat a fixed assembly moti: A machine repeating a fixed motion does not reason or learn. AI means systems that perform tasks that usually need human intelligence.

map.Machine learning is the broader field th: Machine learning is a type of hardware that runs AI programs faster
map.AI only works with images while ML only: AI is a narrow type of machine learning built from fixed rules
map.They mean exactly the same thing in ever: Machine learning needs a person to write each rule, while AI learns from data

ww.Machine learning is a type of hardware t: Machine learning is a method, not hardware. It is one way of building AI in which systems learn from data.
ww.AI is a narrow type of machine learning: This reverses the relationship. AI is the broader field, and machine learning is one approach within it that learns from data.
ww.Machine learning needs a person to write: That swaps them. Machine learning learns patterns from data instead of relying on hand-written rules, and it is one approach within AI.

map.AI that only counts items in a table and: AI that predicts a number, such as next month's sales total
map.AI that only sorts existing files into f: AI that sorts incoming emails into spam and inbox groups
map.AI that only deletes duplicate data from: AI that finds unusual transactions in a bank's records

ww.AI that predicts a number, such as next: Predicting a number is a forecasting task, not creating new content. Generative AI produces new text, images or music from patterns in training data.
ww.AI that sorts incoming emails into spam: Sorting emails into groups is classification of existing items. Generative AI creates new content such as text, images or music.
ww.AI that finds unusual transactions in a: Finding unusual records is anomaly detection and creates nothing new. Generative AI produces new text, images or music.

map.Guaranteed correct decisions in all case: Perfect fairness in the results it gives
map.Freedom from all costs of any kind in a: Setup costs lower than a simple spreadsheet

ww.Perfect fairness in the results it gives: AI can carry bias from its training data, so fair results are not assured. A real benefit is faster analysis of large amounts of data.
ww.Setup costs lower than a simple spreadsh: AI usually costs more to set up, needing data, computing power and skilled staff. A real benefit is faster analysis of large amounts of data.

map.They never make mistakes of any kind in: They work well on tasks unlike their training
map.They understand every situation like a h: They get tired and slow down after long use

ww.They work well on tasks unlike their tra: Performance drops on tasks unlike the training data, so this is not a strength. A real limitation is dependence on the quality of training data.
ww.They get tired and slow down after long: AI systems do not tire the way people do. A real limitation is that results depend on the quality of their training data.

map.A program that stores files only and can: A program that predicts prices by learning from past sales
map.A program that learns only from raw imag: A program that lets experts chat with each other online

ww.A program that predicts prices by learni: That describes a machine learning model that learns from data. An expert system applies rules gathered from human experts to make decisions.
ww.A program that lets experts chat with ea: That is a communication tool and makes no decisions. An expert system applies rules from human experts to decide or advise.

map.A file that stores one number only on a: A database that holds large tables of raw records
map.A tool that cleans every error in the da: A program that predicts future sales from past data

ww.A database that holds large tables of ra: Raw tables are storage, not a quick view. A dashboard displays key figures and charts at a glance.
ww.A program that predicts future sales fro: Predicting is the job of a forecasting model. A dashboard displays key figures and charts at a glance so performance is easy to monitor.

map.Guaranteed removal of all costs for the: Models that train faster with no usage fees
map.No need for an internet link, as work is: Data that is stored on the user's own laptop
map.Automatic accuracy of every result that: Models that fix their own training data errors

ww.Models that train faster with no usage f: Cloud services charge fees for usage, so there are costs. The real benefit is access to large computing power without buying hardware.
ww.Data that is stored on the user's own la: Cloud data lives on remote servers, not the user's laptop. The benefit is large computing power without buying hardware.
ww.Models that fix their own training data: Cloud platforms supply computing power but do not repair data errors. Accuracy still depends on the data and the model.

map.Run AI without any data of any kind in t: Train very large models on a supercomputer for free
map.Write every line of code by hand, with n: Rewrite the source code of existing AI software

ww.Train very large models on a supercomput: No-code tools do not give free computing power. They let users build simple AI solutions with visual blocks instead of writing programs.
ww.Rewrite the source code of existing AI s: Editing source code requires programming skills. No-code tools let users build simple AI solutions without writing programs.

map.Raises the error on purpose at every ste: Splits the data into training and test groups
map.Deletes the training data after every ro: Adds new features to the data to improve results

ww.Splits the data into training and test g: Splitting data is a preparation step. Gradient descent adjusts model parameters step by step to reduce error.
ww.Adds new features to the data to improve: Adding features is feature engineering. Gradient descent changes model parameters in small steps that lower the error.

map.Models never change after deployment, so: Software licenses expire and stop the model from running
map.Monitoring is required only by law and n: Hardware wears out quickly and corrupts the stored model

ww.Software licenses expire and stop the mo: Licenses are not the reason for monitoring. Real-world data can change, making predictions less accurate over time.
ww.Hardware wears out quickly and corrupts: Stored models do not wear out or corrupt this way. Monitoring is needed because real-world data can change and lower accuracy.

map.One that suggests random items only, cho: One that suggests items similar in description to what the user viewed
map.One that suggests items by price only, l: One that suggests the items that sold best this week

ww.One that suggests items similar in descr: That is content-based filtering, which compares item features. Collaborative filtering uses the preferences of users with similar tastes.
ww.One that suggests the items that sold be: Suggesting best sellers uses overall popularity, not personal taste. Collaborative filtering recommends items liked by users with similar tastes.

map.Publishing every customer's details onli: Backing up customer records so they can be restored after a failure
map.Keeping data in a locked room only and n: Making sure stored data is accurate and kept up to date in the system

ww.Backing up customer records so they can: Backups protect against data loss, which is availability. Data privacy means protecting personal information from misuse or from being seen by the wrong people.
ww.Making sure stored data is accurate and: That describes data quality. Data privacy means protecting personal information from being misused or seen by the wrong people.

map.Anonymous data always contains names, so: Anonymous data is stored on public servers where search engines copy it freely
map.Anonymous data is never stored anywhere,: The people in the data later give their names to the researchers who study it

ww.Anonymous data is stored on public serve: Where data is stored is not the cause. Re-identification happens when details such as birth date, zip code and gender are combined to single someone out.
ww.The people in the data later give their: Researchers do not need names from participants. Combining details like birth date, zip code and gender can single someone out.

map.A report about data quality that is sent: A rule that limits how long a company may keep customer records on file
map.A planned backup of the data that is run: A software update that fixes errors in a program used by the staff

ww.A rule that limits how long a company ma: That describes a retention policy, which is a planned rule. A data breach is an incident where private data is accessed or exposed without permission.
ww.A software update that fixes errors in a: Updates are planned maintenance that fix errors. A data breach is an incident in which private data is accessed or exposed without permission.

map.Training on data from one group only, so: Collecting as much data as possible from the easiest sources
map.Never testing the model on any group of: Hiding the data sources from users and testers during review
map.Removing human review entirely, so that: Training until the model scores perfectly on its training data

ww.Collecting as much data as possible from: Volume from easy sources can still miss groups and repeat bias. Reducing bias needs diverse, representative data and tests across groups.
ww.Hiding the data sources from users and t: Hiding sources makes bias harder to spot. Reducing bias needs diverse, representative data and testing results across groups.
ww.Training until the model scores perfectl: A perfect training score suggests overfitting and does not check fairness. Reducing bias needs diverse, representative data and tests across groups.

map.Only the color of the app icon on screen: How many stars the app has in the store
map.Only how many ads appear on the screen: How much storage space the app needs on the phone

ww.How many stars the app has in the store: Star ratings reflect user opinion of features, not data handling. A user should check what data is collected and how it is shared.
ww.How much storage space the app needs on: Storage size says nothing about privacy. A user should check what data is collected and how it is shared.

map.Systems should always be the cheapest to: Systems should return results as fast as the hardware allows
map.Systems should hide how they work from e: Systems should use as much personal data as they can collect

ww.Systems should return results as fast as: Speed is a performance goal, not fairness. Fairness means treating people equitably and avoiding discrimination.
ww.Systems should use as much personal data: Collecting more personal data raises privacy risk and does not ensure equal treatment. Fairness means treating people equitably and avoiding discrimination.

map.Building AI as fast as possible without: Building AI that earns the highest profit for its owners
map.Using AI only to cut costs and to reduce: Using AI that is the newest and most advanced model available

ww.Building AI that earns the highest profi: Profit is a business goal, not a standard of responsibility. Responsible AI is built and used to be safe, fair and accountable.
ww.Using AI that is the newest and most adv: Being the newest says nothing about safety or fairness. Responsible AI is safe, fair and accountable.

map.Only the manager's opinion about the ad: Whether the ad cost more than the one used the previous year
map.Only the color of the ad and the font th: Whether the ad was shown on more channels than competitors used

ww.Whether the ad cost more than the one us: Ad cost does not show what caused the rise. The analyst should check whether other factors, such as seasons or promotions, could explain it.
ww.Whether the ad was shown on more channel: Channel counts compared to competitors do not test other causes. The analyst should check whether seasons, promotions or other factors explain the rise.

map.Ignore it completely for now: Rename one copy of the customer
map.Double every value in the set: Move the copy to a new table

ww.Rename one copy of the customer: Renaming leaves two records for one customer and still double counts them. The standard fix is to remove the duplicate record.
ww.Move the copy to a new table: Moving the copy keeps the customer counted twice across the data. The standard fix is to remove the duplicate record.

ww.Reinforcement learning: Reinforcement learning uses rewards from actions, not labeled examples. Learning from labeled emails is supervised learning.
ww.Rule-based programming: Rule-based programming uses rules written by people instead of learning from examples. Labeled emails make this supervised machine learning.

map.Accuracy is always perfect: It flags too many honest sales
map.It catches all of the fraud: It was tested on too little data

ww.It flags too many honest sales: The model says not fraud for everything, so it flags no honest sales. The problem is that it misses all fraud despite its 99% accuracy.
ww.It was tested on too little data: Test size is not the issue. The 99% score comes from fraud being rare, while the model misses each fraud case.

map.Only the file name matters, as a title i: It sets the file format used for storage
map.Only the file size matters to most analy: It determines how many rows the data set holds
map.It never matters to any analyst or any u: It decides which software opens the data set

ww.It sets the file format used for storage: The source does not set the file format. It matters because it affects reliability, bias and whether the data suits the intended use.
ww.It determines how many rows the data set: Row count comes from collection, not from the source's identity. Source matters because it affects reliability, bias and appropriate use.
ww.It decides which software opens the data: Software choice is unrelated to data quality. The source matters because it affects reliability, bias and appropriate use.

map.Only the total of all the values in the: The correlation between two variables across a dataset
map.Only the mode, the value that appears mo: The frequency of each value in a dataset as bars
map.Only the mean, the sum of the values div: The trend of a variable over time as a line

ww.The correlation between two variables ac: Correlation is shown by a scatter plot. A box plot shows the median, quartiles and potential outliers.
ww.The frequency of each value in a dataset: Bars of value frequencies make a histogram. A box plot shows the median, quartiles and potential outliers.
ww.The trend of a variable over time as a l: A line over time is a line chart. A box plot shows the median, quartiles and potential outliers.

map.They cannot both happen at the same mome: The two events have the same probability of happening
map.They always happen together, so one neve: One event must happen before the other can occur

ww.The two events have the same probability: Equal probability is a different idea; independent events can have different chances. Independence means one outcome does not change the other's probability.
ww.One event must happen before the other c: That describes dependence, where one outcome affects the other. Independent events do not change each other's probability.

map.Independent events that never affect oth: Events whose outcomes do not change each other's odds
map.Events that always happen at the same mo: Events that happen one right after the other

ww.Events whose outcomes do not change each: That describes independent events, which can happen together. Mutually exclusive events cannot happen at the same time.
ww.Events that happen one right after the o: Events in sequence can both occur in a trial. Mutually exclusive events cannot happen at the same time.

map.Correlation always proves cause, as vari: Correlation is measured wrongly when the variables are in different units
map.Causation is impossible to ever show in: Causation is established once the correlation is above 0.5
map.Correlation is random, so it has no link: The variable measured first in time is the cause of the other

ww.Correlation is measured wrongly when the: Correlation works across different units. It does not imply causation because a third factor or chance may explain why variables move together.
ww.Causation is established once the correl: No correlation value establishes causation. A third factor or chance may explain why two variables move together.
ww.The variable measured first in time is t: Order in time does not prove cause. A third factor or chance may explain why two variables move together.

map.The data are clean and free of errors in: The share of people in the group who were surveyed
map.The sample is large enough to include ev: The result can be repeated by the same researcher

ww.The share of people in the group who wer: That describes sampling coverage. Statistical significance is evidence that a result is unlikely to be due to chance.
ww.The result can be repeated by the same r: Repeatability is a separate idea. Statistical significance means a result is unlikely to be due to chance.

map.Making data normal in distribution only: Filling in missing values with the average of each column
map.Deleting outliers from the data and keep: Converting category labels into numbers for a model
map.Encrypting data so that only approved us: Combining records from two tables into one data set

ww.Filling in missing values with the avera: Filling gaps is imputation. Normalization adjusts values to a common scale so features are comparable.
ww.Converting category labels into numbers: That is encoding. Normalization adjusts values to a common scale so features are comparable.
ww.Combining records from two tables into o: Combining tables is a join. Normalization adjusts values to a common scale so features are comparable.

map.Encrypting data so that only approved us: Replacing missing values in a column with the most common value
map.Scaling numbers so that all of them fall: Assigning each category a single number in rank order, such as 1, 2, 3

ww.Replacing missing values in a column wit: That is imputation. One-hot encoding turns a categorical variable into binary columns, one per category.
ww.Assigning each category a single number: That is ordinal or label encoding, which uses one column of ranked numbers. One-hot encoding creates a binary column for each category.

map.Deletes a table and all of the rows that: Adds a new column to one table with a default value
map.Sorts a table by a column and puts the r: Counts the rows in a table and groups them by category

ww.Adds a new column to one table with a de: Adding a column is done with ALTER TABLE. A JOIN combines rows from two or more tables using a related column.
ww.Counts the rows in a table and groups th: Counting and grouping is done with COUNT and GROUP BY. A JOIN combines rows from tables based on a related column.

map.A random guess always, made with no thou: A full search method that tests each possible answer to be sure
map.A proven exact formula that always gives: A rule stored in a database to keep field values valid

ww.A full search method that tests each pos: Testing each possible answer is exhaustive search, which is slow. A heuristic is a practical shortcut that finds a good-enough solution quickly.
ww.A rule stored in a database to keep fiel: That is a validation constraint. A heuristic is a practical shortcut for finding a good-enough solution quickly.

map.Data used for final scoring only, after: Data held back to report the final score of the finished model
map.Data used for the first training only, b: Data used to fit the model's weights during training runs

ww.Data held back to report the final score: That is the test set, kept untouched until the end. A validation set is used to tune model settings during development.
ww.Data used to fit the model's weights dur: That is the training set. A validation set is separate data used to tune model settings during development.

map.Using a more complex model only, and not: Adding more layers to fit the training data better
map.Removing the test set from the data enti: Testing the model on the training data to check progress

ww.Adding more layers to fit the training d: More layers make memorizing noise easier, which increases overfitting. More data, regularization or simpler models reduce it.
ww.Testing the model on the training data t: Testing on training data hides overfitting rather than reducing it. More data, regularization or simpler models reduce overfitting.

map.The data is perfect and has no errors in: The model has learned to find the positive cases
map.Accuracy is always best, as a high score: Accuracy is low when one class is much larger

ww.The model has learned to find the positi: It predicts negative each time, so it finds no positives. The 99% reflects how common negatives are, and accuracy can mislead with imbalanced classes.
ww.Accuracy is low when one class is much l: Accuracy is high here, not low, because the common class is easy to predict. It can be misleading with imbalanced classes.

map.A spreadsheet only, with no tables, keys: A database that stores data in strict tables joined by SQL queries
map.A database with no data in it at all, so: A database that stores data in the cloud instead of on local servers

ww.A database that stores data in strict ta: That describes a relational database. A NoSQL database stores data in flexible formats such as documents or key-value pairs rather than in traditional tables.
ww.A database that stores data in the cloud: Cloud storage is a hosting choice that applies to any database type. NoSQL means data is stored in flexible formats other than traditional tables.

map.The mode is always the largest value: The mode is greater than the mean
